promise: The agent MUST be a primary, co-equal surface (not a bolted-on sidebar) able to occupy a dominant column or the full cockpit, whose actions open and arrange panels as its output.
The agent MUST be terminal-aware — it can read the focused symbol/timeframe/indicators, watchlist, portfolio, and open panels, and can open panels, set symbols, edit the watchlist, and stage actions.

The system MUST present the agent as four explicit intents on stable global hotkeys — Ask (read-only), Edit-panel (focused-panel change), Build (multi-panel/workflow), Delegate (background) — with the active mode visible at all times.
The active persona and active provider/model MUST be visible and switchable by keyboard at any time.
Every capability invocable by the agent MUST also be reachable by hand (palette/menus/panels); no agent-only capability.

After an ambiguous request, the agent MUST do the upfront work and then hand off to the manipulable cockpit — it MUST NOT require the user to do complex multi-object analysis inside the chat transcript.
Hand manipulation MUST take effect immediately and update the shared context the agent reads on its next turn.

Every agent-proposed mutation (panel config, portfolio, multi-panel build, order) MUST be presented as a preview→applied diff with per-item and bulk accept/reject, keyboard-driven; no mutation lands before acceptance.

Order proposals MUST route through the existing §6.5 confirm_and_place boundary (paper-mode default, position limits, read-only/kill-switch checks, append-only audit on accept); there MUST be no auto-apply / 'YOLO' order path.
The §6.5 invariants and Tier-1 LOCKED files MUST be preserved byte-for-byte unless an operator-ratified Tier-4 change is made; the audit suite is a hard gate on any touch.
Read-only MUST be the default for every consumer (internal and external); any mutation is explicit, gated, and audited.

The system MUST maintain a single capability catalog as the source of truth, projected to the internal copilot adapter(s) and the external MCP server, by transformation — no hand-maintained duplicate tool surfaces.
Each catalog entry MUST carry a domain tag and a read_only declaration; the read_only flag MUST drive both the internal mutation gate and the external MCP read-only annotation.
The external MCP surface MUST cover all primary domains (quotes, charts, screener, fundamentals, portfolio, news, quant, brokers-read) by the same tool names the internal copilot uses.

The catalog MUST be complete — every registered handler intended to be agent-reachable MUST have a schema entry (closing the current ~11-handler gap), and the custom-agent allow-list MUST reflect the real catalog.
Multi-round tool use MUST work on every supported provider for a representative two-step task (closing the current Gemini multi-round break).

External MCP access MUST be loopback-only without auth in this scope; any non-loopback exposure is a Tier-4 block-and-ask and is out of scope; the framework MUST be attachable by an external agent (a documented connection path; a discovery file is desirable).
Background ('Delegate') agent runs MUST be bounded by a hard, user-visible ceiling on tokens, spend, wall-clock, and steps; the first breach MUST abort the run with a stated reason.
A background run MUST be visible in an agents rail with status and cost-so-far, and be cancellable and bring-to-foreground-able.
A long run SHOULD checkpoint progress so it can resume, and SHOULD be able to pause for a human-in-the-loop question without losing progress.

The shell MUST be minimal-dark, low-chrome, keyboard-first, dark-only (light theme remains deferred), superseding the warm 'Claude after dark' palette; the canvas palette and CSS tokens MUST be re-skinned together.
The command palette MUST fuzzy-rank panels, commands, symbols, and agents, and MUST surface the keyboard mnemonic for actions it performs.
First run MUST present a minimal, populated starter cockpit (not empty, not every plugin) with the agent surface present; additional panels/plugins open as tabs on demand.
The chrome MUST surface sidecar connection state, active provider/model, and running background agents.

Every data provider, broker, and user-wired connector MUST declare its credentials and shape declaratively; a single BYOK/credentials hub MUST render/mask/test forms generically from those declarations (including a 'needs no key' opt-out and a get-key link/instructions).
The data registry MUST resolve by a standard model key + preference order (replacing the hardcoded asset-class dispatch); every result MUST carry its serving provider as provenance.

Secrets MUST remain in the OS keychain, least-privilege at use (a provider receives only its declared keys, never the whole keychain), never logged/echoed/persisted; storage MUST NOT regress to plaintext files or machine-ID-derived encryption.
Configured connections SHOULD be exportable/importable across machines (secrets via the keychain, not the export file).

The system MUST provide a dedicated settings/preferences surface where effectively every user-facing preference is configurable (keybindings, default agent/persona, default provider/model + preference order, palette behavior, panel defaults, starter-cockpit composition, theming knobs); settings MUST persist locally and be exportable/importable — depth target is Cursor-grade.

Keyboard shortcuts/keybindings MUST be user-remappable from the settings surface, not merely surfaced as mnemonics; conflicting bindings MUST be detected and surfaced; remaps persist locally and travel with the settings export.
Agent claims that assert facts MUST carry citations; data responses MUST carry provenance (which provider served them); the active provider/model/cost MUST be legible on the agent surface.
The system MUST NOT present fabricated or placeholder data as real; unverified or paper/synthetic values MUST be labeled as such.

The read-only broker surface MUST return genuine granular data from the live connected account — distinct, real positions, holdings, P&L, and margins — rather than aliasing them all to a single account summary; this is net-new read implementation; synthetic/paper/disconnected values MUST be clearly labeled; scope stays read-only; the live connected account is reached through an installed broker plugin, not a boot-registered adapter.

The plugin marketplace MUST be the app's primary extensibility model: brokers, data providers/connectors, panels, and agents are all delivered as marketplace plugins the user can install, enable, configure, and remove — one unified extension model.

No broker is hardcoded or registered at boot; the host MUST NOT bootstrap any broker adapter at startup — bootstrap_default_adapters() is retired as the broker entry path; the seven existing plugins/brokers/ plugins MUST become real, installable reference plugins.
The working Kite read-only OAuth logic MUST be kept and repackaged as the first reference broker plugin — not rebuilt from scratch and not a hardcoded default.

The provider-shaped data registry and the plugin contract MUST describe one unified extension model, not two parallel ones: a data provider/connector's declarative credential+shape declaration is the data-source slice of the marketplace plugin model.

The plugin-runtime guarantees the marketplace depends on MUST be real: manifest↔instance id/version checks, requiredHostVersion checks that refuse an incompatible plugin (surfaced, not silently loaded), and working PluginConfig secret resolution.

HARD GUARDRAIL — a broker (or any) plugin MUST NOT be able to bypass the §6.5 boundary: paper-mode default, read-only enforcement, the kill switch, position limits, the diff/accept gate, and append-only audit are all enforced by the host; plugins plug into them and cannot opt out.

Region MUST drive the user-local shape of the product — ticker/exchange resolution, currency, market hours, number/date formatting, and default news/data sources; v1 locale set is US + India (both first-class & deep), GLOBAL best-effort.
